topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I remember that day so clearly, the day I planted the sapling. My hands, small and eager, sinking into the earth, placing that fragile life into the ground with a promise to watch it grow. Years passed, as they tend to do, and with them, the tree flourished. A sturdy oak, it stood as a testament to the passage of time, a silent witness to the evolution of my life. But now, I stand here, staring at the stump, the air heavy with the scent of fresh wood. I can't help but think of the times I could have checked on it, watered it, maybe even put up a fence to protect it. Instead, I let it face the world alone. I wonder how many more years it could have stood, its branches reaching for the sky, if I had just been more vigilant, more attentive.
